overview.description: Tysyacha (Тысяча), meaning 1000 in Russian, is a trick-taking card game popular in Eastern Europe: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Poland and the Baltic states. Three players use a 24-card deck (9 through Ace). Points come from card values and marriages (King-Queen of a suit), which also set trump. First to 1000 points wins.

players.display: 3 active players (4 can play with one sitting out per hand)

overview.deck: 24 cards (9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)

history.origins: Country/Region: Russia (spread to Ukraine, Belarus, Poland, Baltic states). Time period: 19th century. The game combined 17th-century Marriage (King-Queen) trade rules. Polish variant is Tysiąc.
timeline: Present: Popular in Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Poland, Lithuania
history.evolution: Evolved from Marriage-style games; 24-card deck and bidding for declarer.
history.cultural: Widely played in Eastern Europe as a social and family game.

setup.players: 3 active players; 4 can play with one sitting out per hand
setup.deck: 24-card deck: 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each suit. Card values: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, Nine 0.
setup.dealing: Seven cards to each player; three face-down in the center (prikup).

rules.objective: Be the first player to accumulate 1000 points. Points come from card values in tricks and from declaring marriages (King-Queen), which also set the trump suit.
rules.gameplay: Bidding starts at 100, in multiples of five; highest bidder is the taker and picks up the prikup. Trump is initially undefined; players declare marriages when leading to set trump (Hearts 100, Diamonds 80, Clubs 60, Spades 40). Follow suit when possible; win tricks to score.
keyRules: Bidding from 100; taker takes prikup and gives one card to each opponent
Marriages set trump and give bonus points
Follow suit and trump if possible; first to 1000 points wins

strategy.basic: Bid based on hand strength and marriages. You cannot bid over 120 without at least one King-Queen pair. Manage the prikup: after taking it, you may raise your contract; avoid passing a nine to an opponent who might have three (four nines forces a redeal).
strategy.intermediate: Declare marriages when leading to set or change trump; Hearts (100) and Diamonds (80) are most valuable. Time declarations to control trump and maximize points. Remember: 10 beats King in rank. Track card points (120 total in deck) to judge whether you can make your bid.
strategy.advanced: On the barrel (880–999): you have three hands to score at least 120 as declarer to win, or you fall off and lose 120. Use Rospisat' when you cannot make your bid (opponents score 60 each); third Rospisat' costs you 120. Coordinate with defenders only implicitly—each scores separately.
tips: Bidding over 120 requires a marriage; plan bids around declared marriages.
Avoid giving an opponent their fourth nine when discarding after the prikup.
Declare high-value marriages (Hearts, Diamonds) when they secure tricks or trump control.
When on the barrel, prioritize winning the bid and making at least 120.

list.name: Polish Tysiąc (Tysiąc licytowany)
list.description: Polish variant with bidding in multiples of 10, marriages can be announced on first trick, no barrel (instead 'locked' at 900-1000), includes optional 'Bomba' (rospisat equivalent).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in bidding, barrel, and rospisat rules; engine overrides not yet specified.

list.name: Auction 1000 (Two-player)
list.description: Two-player variant where each player receives ten cards and there are two two-card talons. Similar rules to three-player game but with modified dealing and scoring.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Two-player dealing and talon layout require engine overrides to be defined.

list.name: Draw 1000 (Two-player)
list.description: Two-player variant with six cards dealt and twelve-card draw stock. First six tricks have no requirement to follow suit; after stock exhaustion must follow suit and trump.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Draw stock and no-follow-suit phase need engine overrides.

list.name: German 1001 (Tausendeins)
list.description: Simpler German variant using 20-card deck (without nines), bidding in multiples of 10, minimum bid 40. First player to exceed 1000 wins.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Different deck size and scoring threshold need engine overrides.

list.name: Russeln (Austrian)
list.description: Austrian variant with 24 cards, 8 cards dealt to each of three players (no talon), bidding in multiples of 10 with no minimum, must follow suit and beat highest card if possible.
list.emptyOverridesReason: No talon and different deal pattern require engine overrides.

list.name: Gold Set
list.description: Variant starting with three deals where minimum bid is 120 and all scores are doubled. No one succeeds means another gold set is played.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Gold set scoring and minimum bid need engine overrides.

list.name: Blind Bidding
list.description: Player can bid without looking at hand. If blind bid wins, hand is shown, card exchange is face-up, and all scores for the hand are doubled.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Blind bid and doubled scoring need engine overrides.

list.name: Dark Talon
list.description: Bidder picks up prikup cards without showing them to other players before exchanging.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Prikup visibility rule needs engine override.

list.name: Four Aces Combination
list.description: Some players award 200 points for announcing a set of four aces (must win trick first, then lead one ace while holding the other three).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Four aces bonus scoring needs engine override.

list.name: Limited Rospisat'
list.description: Some regions allow only two Rospisat' declarations per game, or allow one Rospisat' and one Spisat' (declarer loses bid value but opponents score zero).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rospisat and Spisat limits need engine overrides.

list.name: Modified Barrel Rules
list.description: Variations include: different barrel level (850, 870, 900), multiple players on barrel simultaneously, indefinite barrel time, or multiple jumps cause score reset to zero.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Barrel level and penalty rules need engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Simplified bidding and basic trick-following without marriage optimization.
difficulty.medium: Strategic marriage timing to control trump suit and track total card points available.
difficulty.hard: Advanced barrel play, Rospisat' risk management, and implicit opponent coordination.

considerations: Bidding: estimate hand strength and marriage potential; model opponents' bids.
Marriage timing: decide when to declare to set or change trump.
Trick play: follow suit, trump when unable; track remaining cards and points.
Barrel and Rospisat': when to risk bid vs concede; opponent zero-count and Rospisat' limits.

hero.subtitle: Tysyacha
hero.tagline: The ultimate Eastern European marriage trick-taking challenge.

synthesis.shortDescription: Tysyacha (1000) is a competitive trick-taking game for three players using a 24-card deck. Players bid for the right to take a talon, declare marriages to set trumps, and race to be the first to reach 1000 points.

prompts.ai: Tysyacha is a 3-player trick-taking game. Bid to take the prikup, declare marriages to set trump, and score points from card values and declarations to reach 1000 first. Note the barrel rule at 880 points.

scoring.description: Points from cards in tricks and marriage bonuses. Ace=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0. Marriages: Hearts=100, Diamonds=80, Clubs=60, Spades=40.
scoring.winCondition: Reach 1000 points. Special barrel rules apply when score is between 880 and 1000.

penalties.failed_bid: Value of bid is subtracted from score.
penalties.rospisat: 120 point penalty on every 3rd conceded game.
